basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 16.' and it opens 'Vers. 16. Generatione quarta revertentur huc. Moyses dicit: quinta generatione egressi'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 16. Generatione quarta revertentur huc. Moyses dicit: quinta generatione egressi sunt filii Israel de Aegypto. Hic vero dicit: generatione quarta. Sed utrumque verum est. Nam si per Levi computes, quartam inventes generationem ita: Levi, Caaz, Caaz genuit Amram, Amram genuit Aaron, Aaron genuit Eleazar, Eleazar genuit Phinees. Caaz ingressus | est Aegyptum cum patre suo Levi: Phinees vero filius Eleazari ingressus est terram repromissionis. Si vero et quomodo quinta generatione hoc factum sit velis scire, per Judam computare debebis. Judas genuit Phares, Phares genuit Esrom, Esrom genuit Aminadab, Aminadab genuit Naason, Naason genuit Salmon. Judas ingressus est cum filio suo Phares in Aegyptum. Naason vero princeps fuit tribus Judae in deserto, cujus filius intravit in terram promissionis.
